name: Pontcysyllte Aqueduct and Canal
countries: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
description: In northeast Wales, Thomas Telford's Pontcysyllte Aqueduct carries narrowboats on a cast-iron trough held up by 19 stone arches, high above the River Dee. Finished in 1805, it is the longest aqueduct in Britain and the highest canal aqueduct in the world. Walk or cruise across the narrow towpath for dizzying views down the Vale of Llangollen.
